source_evidence: At D326~14:32 V says exactly 'I want to find out what is so important that people have to die to keep the operation running'. Coxswain takes the concern seriously but distinguishes Quenwood's killings from her own firsthand knowledge of illicit ferry freight; she cannot attribute murders to the current operation or its other participants. She says the extra freight has been carried on some late passenger runs, and the publicly announced last passenger sailing is at16:00 today (newly fixed ordinary local schedule before any observation; not confirmation of an illicit pickup, receiver, or active transfer). She indicates the public steps overlooking the assessment landing as a lawful place to watch the boats without boarding or endangering passengers. Cirren supports observing first; will protect passengers and seek evidence rather than presuming guilt. Coxswain is willing to continue conversation but has not supplied confidential cooperation, a specific smuggling schedule, identification, or promise to assist seizure. V has not promised anything or selected a surveillance location, boarded, arranged a skiff, or accepted any further commitment. No roll; ordinary information and existing public access. No elapsed rest or resource changes. Await V's choice. All earlier knowledge, custody and obligations preserved.
pending_action: D326~14:32 public quay at Orsaven ferry landing, V/Mara/Cirren/Fenar with ferry coxswain speaking away from loading crew; coach/four horses safely at Copper Hart. Player exact 'Lets find out shall we' authorizes Cirren's suggested voluntary inquiry into unusual evening freight with the coxswain, not a voyage, seizure, pledge, expenditure, coercion or accepted further task. Coxswain is experienced working crew leader, concerned for ordinary passengers' safe return and workers' wages. She dismisses deckhands to finish ordinary loading, voluntarily acknowledges from her own experience that on selected evening runs cases are transferred aboard from another boat before assessment landing, some crew knowingly carry goods without ordinary customs processing. Has seen fine imported lace in cases; does not claim to know upstream supplier, hidden syndicate, bribe recipients or Quenwood's murders beyond public case. She is willing to discuss a later run and actual sailing information if V explains intention and assures that passengers can clear safely before intervention. No new sailing time, active transfer, inspection rota, cargo schedule or actual recipient fixed/revealed. Cirren independently says the fraud cannot be recovered by endangering passengers and wants to learn who arranged the payments; no pledge beyond his power. No uncertain promise yet, no persuasion roll, no crew warning, no threat, no commitment or confrontation. Paymaster's disclosed48gp balance retained pending lawful restitution, notification promised not confirmed sent. Original ferry guarantee and records in respective custodians' custody; no duplicate historic claim. Quenwood life sentence upheld, identified assets frozen, restitution distribution pending. Boatyard skiff freed, jelly defeated, daughter referral to Meret delivered; no new business contract.
